extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) and Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs) under 37 CFR (including when CPAs are improper and treated as RCEs), including required fees, submissions, responsiveness, new matter, appeal/post-allowance consequences, and form paragraph usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of amendments with RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to file all amendments no later than the filing of the RCE to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.03(a). If amendments are filed after RCE filing they risk disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action with RCE when more time needed
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional time is needed to prepare and file a supplement (e.g., affidavit or declaration containing test data) to the previously filed submission, applicant should consider filing a suspension of action by the Office under 37 CFR 1.103(c) with the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 709 for more details on suspension of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for new/excess claims with RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: New claims in excess of the number previously paid for, which are filed with the RCE or thereafter, will require payment of the appropriate fees under 37 CFR 1.16; applicant does not need to pay a fee for excess claims previously paid for prior to the filing of the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess claims already paid before RCE: no additional fee. New excess claims filed with/after RCE: pay per 37 CFR 1.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA ineligibility based on filing date (May 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: CPA practice under 37 CFR 1.53(d) does not apply to applications (other than design) if the prior application has a filing date on or after May 29, 2000; a CPA must have an actual filing date before May 29, 2000 to be filed for that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date used for identification is that of the prior application, but the CPA's filing date is the date the request for CPA is filed (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)). A CPA filed on/after May 29, 2000 (except design) is not permitted under 1.53(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treated as RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPA of an application (other than design) is filed on or after May 29, 2000 (to which CPA practice no longer applies), the Office will automatically treat the improper CPA as an RCE of the prior application (identified in the request for CPA) under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CPA does not satisfy requirements of 37 CFR 1.114 (e.g., lacks submission under 1.114(b) or fee under 1.17(e)), it will still be treated as an (improper) RCE and time periods set in the last Office action will continue to run; if time expired, applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 to revive abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to convert improper CPA to a 1.53(b) application
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who does not want an improper CPA treated as an RCE may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) requesting conversion to an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.53(e) must include: (A) $130 petition fee; (B) a true copy of the complete nonprovisional application as filed; (C) any amendments entered in the prior nonprovisional application; (D) any amendments submitted but not entered that were directed to be entered; (E) an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 if not already submitted. The Office will not grant the petition unless before an appropriate deciding official before an Office action has been mailed in response to the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.42.15 for CPA treated as RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.42.15 should be used by the examiner to inform applicant that a CPA is being treated as an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 7.42.15 text acknowledges CPA is being treated as continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 and cites statutory changes and eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality upon timely RCE with submission and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files an RCE with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission, the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action to which a reply is outstanding and the submission will be entered and considered (37 CFR 1.114(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is under final rejection, the submission must meet reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111 to continue prosecution. Mere request and fee will not toll running of time unless a timely submission meeting 1.111 is received. Use form paragraph 7.42.04 to notify applicant that finality withdrawn and submission entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of an RCE submission
rubrics_metrics.description: As set forth in 37 CFR 1.114, a submission may include an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submission does not comply with 1.111, use form paragraph 7.42.08 (not 7.42.04). Previously submitted arguments may count as a submission if they are responsive within meaning of 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for continued examination under 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility test is repeatedly referenced for use of form paragraphs and for determining proper/improper RCE treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submissions must be bona fide attempts
rubrics_metrics.description: If reply to a final Office action is outstanding and the submission is not fully responsive to the final Office action, then it must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the final Office action in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bona fide, inform applicant why not fully responsive and give a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever longer) to complete reply (37 CFR 1.135(c)), using form paragraph 7.42.08. If not bona fide, treat RCE as improper and prepare Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051). An IDS alone is an example of not being a bona fide attempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of an improper RCE (no submission/fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the RCE is improper (lacking required submission under 1.114(b) or fee under 1.17(e)), the RCE will not toll the period for reply and the application will be abandoned after the statutory period if no compliant submission is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and mail Form PTO-2051 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE)'; if application is under appeal and missing items, follow form paragraphs 7.42.10-7.42.14 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition for RCE amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(a) provides that '[n]o amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention.' Any amendment entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 that is determined to contain new matter should be treated in the same manner that a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 determined to contain new matter is currently treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant seeks to add new matter, the procedure in 37 CFR 1.114 is not available; applicant must file a continuation-in-part under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Also, because 35 U.S.C. 132(b) and 37 CFR 1.114 provide continued examination of an application (not a continuing application), an applicant cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from those previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., cannot 'switch inventions') (see 37 CFR 1.145). See MPEP § 706.03(o) for handling new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action final after filing RCE: conditions and statutory periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The action immediately subsequent to the filing of an RCE with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114 may be made final only if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b) for making a first action final in a continuing application are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.09 if appropriate. A shortened statutory period for reply to this final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from mailing date; interplay rules if a first reply filed within TWO MONTHS and advisory action delayed; in no event will statutory period expire later than SIX MONTHS from mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of RCE after allowance or Quayle action
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE with fee and a submission in an application which has been allowed, prosecution will be reopened. However, if the issue fee has been paid, payment of the fee for an RCE and a submission without a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue will not avoid issuance of the application as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RCE filed before issue fee paid: petition under 1.313 not required. If RCE filed after issue fee paid and a petition under 1.313 is filed and granted, applicant does not have to pay the issue fee again if application is thereafter allowed. If issue fee paid and prosecution reopened, no refund of issue fee; applicant may request previously submitted issue fee be applied toward new notice of allowance. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but before Board decision withdraws appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 after the filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution of the application before the examiner (see 37 CFR 1.114(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing of an RCE under 1.114 in an application on appeal awaiting decision will be treated as a withdrawal of the appeal regardless of whether the RCE includes the fee or a submission. Applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed; otherwise the Board may refuse to vacate a decision. Use form paragraph 7.42.06 to notify applicant that appeal withdrawn and prosecution reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling RCE on appeal lacking fee/submission — no claims allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 filed after appeal that lacks the fee and/or the submission and where no claim is allowed: the appeal is withdrawn and the application is abandoned (proceedings as to rejected claims terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.10 when appropriate; see MPEP § 1215.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling RCE on appeal lacking submission but at least one claim allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE including the fee was filed after appeal but lacks the submission required by 1.114 and there is at least one allowed claim, the appeal is withdrawn and the application will be passed to issue on the allowed claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.11. Cancel claims that are dependent upon rejected claims as necessary. See MPEP § 1215.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling RCE on appeal lacking submission with formal matters outstanding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the RCE lacks the required submission but allowed claim(s) exist and formal matters outstanding, the application will be passed to issue on allowed claim(s) provided outstanding formal matters are corrected within a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.12; identify formal matters to be corrected and allow extensions under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling RCE on appeal lacking fee but including submission; claim allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE including a submission was filed after appeal but lacks the fee required by 37 CFR 1.17(e), the submission has not been entered and the appeal is withdrawn; since proceedings as to rejected claims are terminated and at least one claim is allowed, the application will be passed to issue on allowed claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.13. Note the submission is not entered per 37 CFR 1.116(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling RCE on appeal lacking fee with formal matters outstanding
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE including a submission was filed after appeal but lacks the fee and there are allowed claims with outstanding formal matters, the application will be passed to issue on allowed claim(s) provided the formal matters are corrected within a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.14; explain formal matters in bracket and allow extensions under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper RCE after Board decision before further appeal or civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an RCE (accompanied by the fee and a submission) after a decision by the Board but before filing a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action will result in withdrawal of the action's finality and the submission being considered; however a Board decision is res judicata and arguments without amendment or new facts will not remove such rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.07. See MPEP §§ 706.03(w) and 1214.01 for limits of argument after Board decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after Board decision (no submission/fee) — notification
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but before further appeal and the RCE lacks the fee and/or submission, the examiner should notify the applicant that the RCE is improper using form paragraph 7.42.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If time for seeking court review has passed without review, include the form paragraph with a Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment; if time remains, use PTOL-90. Do not set a time period. If a submission is filed but fee missing, state whether submission has been entered (generally it should not be entered unless the amendment obviously places application in condition for allowance with supervisory approval). If application not eligible (not utility/plant filed on/after June 8, 1995), use Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051) prepared by technical support personnel. After time for court review has passed, examiner must take up application for consideration (see MPEP § 1214.06).
